references.text: The Lord refers to himself as the 'source of living water' that the people have abandoned. The expression 'living water' (τὸ ὕδωρ τὸ ζῶν) has its background in this Old Testament motif, which Jeremiah uses concerning God himself ([ref:Jer 2:13|Jeremiah 2:13]).

"Those who turn away from you shall be written in the dust, for they have forsaken the source of living water, the Lord." Jeremiah again points to the Lord as the source of living water—the same expression Jesus uses about himself toward the amazed woman ([ref:Jer 17:13|Jeremiah 17:13]).

"You shall draw water with joy from the springs of salvation." Isaiah speaks of living water from God's salvation. The verb 'draw' (ἀντλέω) directly resonates with the woman's question about a drawing bucket (ἄντλημα) in John 4:11 ([ref:Isa 12:3|Isaiah 12:3]).
Zechariah's prophecy that living water shall flow out from Jerusalem. The expression 'living water' points forward to what Jesus offers the Samaritan woman ([ref:Zech 14:8|Zechariah 14:8]).

Jacob meets Rachel at the well. Jacob's Well, mentioned in John 4:6, is directly linked to the patriarch Jacob, and the well motif forms the background for the woman's question about this deep well ([ref:Gen 29:1-12|Genesis 29:1-12]).

The Lord commands Moses to gather the people at the well and promises to give them water. The well from which God gives water forms the background for Jesus' offer of living water—an offer that amazes the woman ([ref:Num 21:16-18|Numbers 21:16-18]).

The woman continues her misunderstanding from verse 11 and asks, "You are not greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well, are you?" She still does not understand whom she is speaking to ([ref:John 4:12|John 4:12]).

Jesus answers the woman's amazement by explaining that the water he gives will become a spring welling up to eternal life. The woman's question in verse 11 finds its answer here ([ref:John 4:14|John 4:14]).

Jesus cries out in the temple, "Let anyone who is thirsty come to me and drink!" Here Jesus further develops the motif of living water as a gift of the Spirit—the same water the woman wondered about ([ref:John 7:37-39|John 7:37-39]).
"I will give the one who is thirsty from the spring of the water of life as a gift." Revelation completes the motif of the living water that Jesus offers ([ref:Rev 21:6|Revelation 21:6]).
